findings.problem: finish() publishes complete bank.json before wrapper computes its file_ref, writes trial_bank_producer into hpo.json, and runs final original checkpoint. Any OSError or deadline/observation failure at these later operations escapes through context reset only, leaving the completed index with admitted objectives discoverable.
source_counterexample: Existing actual cold HPO succeeds; at least one valid trial admitted.
finish() and its internal _exclusive return successfully, publishing bank.json.
Next file_ref checkpoint or HPO atomic_json/final checkpoint raises the original error.
The wrapper finally resets context but has no owned-index revocation branch; bank.json remains.
findings.why_existing_rollback_and_fixture_do_not: _exclusive revokes only errors caught before that particular call returns. The current late-index test injects fsync inside finish, not the subsequent caller operations.
findings.impact: Contradicts complete-index/no-positive-bank-on-late-I/O-or-original-budget-failure contract. No consumer exists and reuse_eligible stays false, so this is a producer finalization evidence defect, not an observed cache hit or ML failure.
findings.minimal_prospective_repair: After root authorization, preserve frozen R2. A new narrow revision should retain exact owned index inode/ref and revoke that same completed index on any post-finish handoff/hash/HPO-write/final-check failure; never delete unrelated/preexisting files. Preserve original raised type/traceback and separate cleanup secondary types; no new clock, allowance, consumer or model change.
meaningful_source_contracts: Inject post-finish index hash/check failure and assert no complete discoverable index.
